entries.not_relevant_because: Neither manuscript says anything about higher signatures, the L-class pairing ⟨L(M) ∪ f*x, [M]⟩, or homotopy invariance. 'Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality' proves that the rational fundamental class maps to zero in H_n(Bπ;Q) for manifolds with positive scalar curvature, a conclusion about scalar curvature that does not involve L-classes. 'An integral scalar curvature bound for real simplicial volume' concerns the integral of negative scalar curvature against simplicial volume. The only occurrence of 'higher signatures' in either manuscript is a bibliography title.

entries.not_relevant_because: Neither manuscript treats whether aspherical manifolds with isomorphic fundamental groups are homeomorphic, nor whether homotopy equivalences between them are homotopic to homeomorphisms. Their aspherical content is that closed aspherical manifolds admit no positive scalar curvature metric (Corollary 'The Gromov–Lawson aspherical conjecture') and that every nonnegative scalar curvature metric on one is flat (Corollary 'Aspherical nonnegative-scalar-curvature rigidity'). The flatness conclusion is a metric rigidity statement, not a topological one. The integral-bound paper does not discuss aspherical manifolds at all.
read: both build/ folders, all sections, searched by grep for aspherical, homeomorph, rigidity, Borel conjecture
